title: A Radio Segment on Staying Humble After Success
script: Narrator: [reflective] Last month, I won an award at work for the best sales results in our entire branch, and honestly, it changed something inside me temporarily.
Narrator: [honestly] For about a week, I felt proud in a way that started to feel uncomfortable, even to myself when I noticed it happening.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I found myself mentioning the award in almost every conversation, even when nobody had actually asked me about it at all.
Narrator: [reflective] One afternoon, my colleague Dedi quietly told me that I had been talking about the award constantly since the ceremony happened.
Narrator: [honest] At first, I felt embarrassed and slightly defensive, because I didn't like hearing that about myself from someone I respected.
Narrator: [thoughtful] But later that evening, I thought about it seriously, and I realized he was completely right about how I had been behaving.
Narrator: [reflective] I remembered that the award wasn't only because of my own effort. My team supported me through every difficult negotiation this year.
Narrator: [honestly] My manager also gave me opportunities that other people never received, simply because of good timing and circumstances beyond my control.
Narrator: [thoughtful] So although I had worked hard, plenty of other people work just as hard without ever receiving recognition or an award.
Narrator: [determined] The next morning, I apologized to Dedi for talking so much about myself, and I thanked my team properly for the first time.
Narrator: [warmly] Their reaction surprised me. Several people said they had been waiting to hear something like that since the ceremony happened.
Narrator: [reflective] I understood then that humility isn't pretending your achievement didn't matter. It's remembering how many people helped you reach it.
Narrator: [gently] Success can quietly change how you treat others if you're not paying close attention to yourself and your own behavior.
Narrator: [peacefully] Now, when I feel proud of something, I try to pause and ask who else deserves credit alongside me for it.
Narrator: [warmly] That small question keeps me grounded, and honestly, it has made my relationships at work noticeably warmer than they were before.
Narrator: [with a small smile] The award still sits on my desk, but these days, it reminds me of my team, not just of myself alone.
